Chapter one
Selene
 
Birthdays weren't really a big deal for me.
 
But for my twenty-fifth birthday, I wanted to do something completely out of character that would leave everyone's gaze on the floor. I wore a crimson silk dress that hugged every curve of my body, making my skin look stark white against the bold fabric.
 
At 7 p.m., I walked into the largest club in the city..
 
The indoor pool, the she-wolves in bikinis, the passionate kissing, and the deafening music made me instantly uncomfortable, but I endured it. After all, this was a birthday party that Xavier had specially organized for me.
 
After asking around, I finally found Xavier’s private room and thankfully it was much quieter than the noisy, bustling chaos outside, which let me breathe a little easier.
 
Just as I was about to push open the door, a loud laugh came from inside.
 
"Wow, Xavier, you actually reeled her in after half a year? I thought a chaste, virtuous woman like Selene wouldn't be seduced by you. I admit defeat this time. I'll transfer a hundred thousand to your account tonight."
 
Another guy laughed. "You're already conceding before you've even reached base? I don't care, I'm only giving in when it's confirmed tomorrow morning."
 
The room filled with rowdy laughter, but the world around me went eerily quiet. I stared blankly at the doorknob, all my warmth I felt and was feeling gradually turning to ice.
 
The discussions inside didn't stop though.
 
"Is Young Master Xavier really planning to sleep with her and then dump her? Selene might be an omega from the outer territories, but she's still the academy beauty. Perfect figure, top grades, and most importantly—she's still untouched."
 
"Her family is poor, from a low-ranking rogue lineage by the way. No matter how good she is, a girl like that is only meant to be played with."
 
I felt my blood boil and my stomach churn. I trembled slightly, my nails digging deep into my palms as I took sharp breaths to suppress my rising fury. But when I heard that familiar voice, I couldn't hold back anymore.
 
"It's hard to say," Xavier said. "I'm not in a rush to choose a fated mate. I can play around for another two years."
 
I threw the door open with a loud click, the faint hallway glow shone directly on me, making the red dress dazzlingly bright in the dim room.
 
The sounds inside abruptly stopped.
 
Xavier looked toward the door, his smug expression freezing for a split second. Then, he stood up with a smooth smile, acting as if nothing had happened. "Why did you come up here by yourself? I was just about to go down and pick you up."
 
I didn't let myself show a single shred of emotion. I just kept a casual, contemptuous smile on my lips. "Do you know why you couldn't seduce me in half a year, Xavier? Because I'm a germaphobe, and your scent is too freaking dirty."
 
Xavier stood there, stunned, until I turned and disappeared down the hall. Only then did he snap out of his daze, clenching his fists tightly. He grabbed a wine glass from the table and smashed it violently on the floor, furious. "Selene!"
 
~~~
 
Everything went to shit after that but when I left there, I didn't go home immediately. Instead, I went into a nearby rogue-friendly bar. It wasn't that I was intentionally trying to get blackout drunk. I just had nothing else to do, so I ordered a pitcher of liquor and sipped it slowly, watching the lively crowd on the dance floor like an outsider. I finally left, staggering unsteadily, when I almost fell asleep in my seat.
 
As I passed a traffic light, I spotted an SUV that looked structurally like Xavier’s, but when I got closer, I saw that it wasn't.
 
But still, a vehicle like this could only be bought by someone with terrifying power, not to mention that the design was incredibly sleek. Older Alphas generally didn't drive this kind of car. At that moment, under the heavy influence of the alcohol, a twisted desire for revenge flared up in my heart.
 
I stepped forward and knocked firmly on the dark window and someone rolled down the window.
 
I pulled on the handle, ready to get into the passenger seat.
 
He must have caught the faint scent of alcohol on me, and seeing that the red light was about to change, he unlocked the door and let me scramble inside.
 
"Xavier isn't with you?" his deep, authoritative baritone filled the car. "I'll have him come pick you up."
 
I panicked the second I heard Xavier's name, completely forgetting to wonder why the driver of a random car knew about my relationship with him. But I was too drunk to care.
 
I gripped his arm tightly, though I forced my tone to sound completely nonchalant. "We broke up."
 
"Then I'll take you home. Where is your pack-house?"
 
After a long moment, having received no reply from me, his turned his head and smiled meaningfully.
 
~~~
 
I vaguely felt someone carry me and lay me down on a massive bed. I forced my eyes halfway open and met a pair of piercing, starry eyes.
 
'He looks dangerously good,' I thought to myself.
 
The man exuded a terrifyingly noble aura, his broad arms brimming with raw, masculine Lycan strength. Unlike Xavier’s boyish charm, this man was mature and deadly—clearly someone who walked the highest echelons of power and wealth in the supernatural world. He was like a walking hormonal poison, capable of captivating a she-wolf without her even realizing it.
 
'Is it just my imagination? Why does he look so familiar?'
 
I stared intently, my eyes misty with unshed tears, my cheeks flushed with a drunken blush. I looked captivating, yet my wide eyes remained pure and gentle.
 
His voice carried a low, warning growl. "What you're doing right now is dangerous."
 
Drunk and confused, I didn't care about the danger. I wrapped my arms tightly around his waist, looking both innocent and completely clingy.
 
His Adam's apple bobbed. With a low sound, he rolled onto the bed, pinning my hands flat above my head. His deep voice carried a dangerous hint of seduction. "Who am I?"
 
I sniffed the air weakly, my eyes sparkling under his weight. "You smell very nice... like cedar and frost."
 
His chest tightened. He freed one hand, violently loosening his tie and tossing it aside, then leaned down and kissed me tenderly. His kisses traveled from my lips to my jaw, then down to my ear, tasting me slowly, carefully trying to control his rhythm. But a hint of his usual, icy clarity remained in his eyes.
 
A tingling sensation shot through my entire body. I unconsciously murmured a soft, tender whimper, a sound so gentle it completely shattered his restraint when it hit his ears.
 
I felt as if I were on a roller coaster, my heart pounding wildly back and forth. Then, a sharp pain brought me back to my senses for a single, gasping moment, followed by a hazy, dreamlike feeling as if I were floating on clouds.
 
When I finally opened my eyes again, it was broad daylight.
 
But waking up brought an endless, crushing wave of regret.
 
Yes, I was filled with deep, sickening regret. A perfectly rational woman had made a terrible mistake and given herself to a stranger on a drunken whim. I wanted to slap myself.
 
"You're awake."
 
My body tensed instantly, and my heart pounded like a war drum. But my mind immediately locked onto a decision: things had already gone this far, and I was the one who had taken the initiative, so I had to preserve the absolute last bit of my dignity.
 
I sat up, pulling the covers over myself and forcing a calm, composed face, though I was inwardly cursing my own stupidity. "Last night... it was consensual. And we'll never see each other again."
 
Unfortunately, my voice choked up before I could finish the sentence. My gaze finally focused on the man's face, and my mind reeled as if struck by lightning.
 
The towering, slender figure, the unapproachable aura, and that calm, analytical gaze left me completely bewildered.
 
I had met Killian once a few months ago at a high-ranking pack summit, but mature Alphas with an ascetic, deadly air always leave a deep impression. I remembered him instantly.
 
This was Xavier’s older cousin. He was the Supreme Alpha of the entire Northern Coalition—the most ruthless legal and martial authority in the werewolf world. He was completely invincible in pack tribunals and enjoyed a terrifying reputation.
 
This man, revered as an unfeeling god by the packs, was so calm and wise right now that I couldn't even reconcile him with the wolfish, aggressive predator from last night.
 
It was completely outrageous.
 
I suddenly felt dizzy. I instinctively braced myself against the mattress, and the obviously oversized silk pajamas he had put me in slipped down my shoulders, revealing a glimpse of my chest.
 
I hurriedly pulled the collar back up, my face burning with acute embarrassment—entirely unaware that the man sitting by the bed was giving me a much deeper look.
 
"So, you gave your virginity to me, your ex's Alpha cousin, just to get revenge on Xavier? You've got some wild ideas, little wolf." Killian tapped his fingers lightly against his knee, his expression completely unreadable.
 
I looked up, half embarrassed and half annoyed. "I didn't know it was you last night!"
 
Killian’s dark eyes slid over my slender shoulders and neck. He adjusted his collar, reached over to the nightstand, and slid a financial pack settlement draft toward me.
 
"This was your first time, and I am aware of that," he said, his voice dropping into a chilling, professional detachment. "But I cannot take responsibility for you. Consider this five million credits as my compensation. If it's not enough to buy your silence, we can discuss it further."
 
The cold, heartless words sent a violent chill straight down my spine, turning my flushed face deathly pale.
 
Noticing the sudden change in my expression, Killian added, his face a mask of stone, "Be smart, Selene. From your perspective, it is the wisest thing to do to accept the funds and walk away."
 
It was a blatant reminder to recognize my own status, to have absolutely no illusions about a mating bond, and to take the payout like a clean cash transaction.
 
Underneath the covers, my hands gripped my thigh so tightly that my nails nearly drew blood, barely managing to suppress the suffocating humiliation.
 
I forced a sharp, radiant smile onto my face. I reached over to my small bag on the nightstand, took out a single, crumpled one-dollar pack coin, and slapped it squarely into Killian's large palm.
 
I looked right into his eyes, making my gaze as alluring and careless as possible. "Keep your money, Alpha. You did a decent job last night. Consider that your tip."
 
Killian’s brow furrowed sharply. He paused, his icy composure cracking for a fraction of a second as he stared at the coin. Then he stood up, his expression completely detached again. "I won't say anything about this to Xavier."
 
I clenched my teeth, forcing myself to hold it together until I had finally left his private estate gates behind me. Only then did I let go, my mouth already filled with the bitter, metallic taste of my own blood.

Chapter two
Selene
 
What an asshole!
 
After fleeing his estate, I went straight back to my small apartment, cleaned myself up, and tried to wash the scent of cedar and winter frost off my skin. Even though last night had been an absolute nightmare, I still had a job to do and I couldn’t afford to miss a shift.
 
But to my utter shock, the moment I stepped into my local pack outpost, my supervisor handed me an immediate transfer notice. I was being ordered to report to the Northern Coalition Enforcer Headquarters right away to provide emergency administrative support.
 
As it turned out, my small territory outpost wasn’t entirely disconnected from Killian. Our local branch was a direct subsidiary under the jurisdiction of the Supreme Enforcer Office.
 
Moving up to headquarters would normally be a dream come true for a low-ranking omega like me. But I hesitated for a split second, my heart hammering against my ribs. But then I reasoned with myself—headquarters was a massive, sprawling fortress.
 
The chances of a someone grunt like me bumping into the Supreme Alpha Enforcer himself were practically zero. I readily accepted the reassignment. Besides, the orders emphasized that the situation was critical, so I shifted into high gear and caught a shuttle straight to the main citadel.
 
They weren’t kidding about it being urgent.
 
The moment I arrived at headquarters, before I could even finish my basic onboarding paperwork, an HR she-wolf shoved a massive stack of case files into my arms. She told me to get straight to the strategic war room because the high-level project briefing was starting right that second.
 
The HR department was completely overwhelmed dealing with a sudden influx of regional transfers and didn't have time to guide me, so I had to navigate the stone corridors of the fortress myself. By the time I finally located the massive briefing hall, it was already packed to the brim with elite warriors and pack analysts.
 
Fortunately, the commanding project manager hadn’t arrived yet. I quietly slipped through the heavy rear doors and took a seat at the very back of the room, trying to blend into the shadows.
 
"Were you transferred from the outer branch?" a wolf sitting next to me whispered, eyeing my uniform.
 
I nodded quickly, setting the heavy files on the desk. "I just rushed over from the border. What kind of case is so urgent?" I pointed to a bottle of mountain spring water sitting on the table. "Can I drink this?" My throat was parched from the lingering heat of the alcohol.
 
My new colleague nodded enthusiastically and immediately began whispering a breakdown of the rogue pack incursions we were tracking.
 
I took a long, grateful gulp of water, listening closely, when suddenly the heavy double doors at the front of the room swung open. Instinctively, I looked up. My eyes slammed right into a pair of chillingly indifferent, piercing starry eyes.
 
"Pfft—!"
 
I choked violently, spraying a mouthful of water right across my desk, coughing and wheezing uncontrollably.
 
The sheer volume of my choking fit instantly drew the sharp gazes of every single elite warrior in the front rows. But the moment they realized who had just walked into the room, they collectively stiffened and snapped their heads back straight, fixing their eyes forward.
 
The entire briefing hall plummeted into a suffocating, dead silence, save for my pathetic, echoing coughs.
 
I forced down the burning discomfort in my throat, my face flushing a deep, mortified crimson as I stared incredulously at the front of the room. Sitting at the head of the massive obsidian war table, radiating absolute command as our project commander, was Killian.
 
It was like seeing a literal ghost.
 
Images of our tangled limbs from last night flashed through my mind in an uncontrollable rush—the bruising kisses, the possessive grip of his hands, his dark, heavy growls, and those low, intoxicating whispers. Just the memory was enough to make my skin burn.
 
Yet here he was. The man who had been a lawless predator hours ago was now sitting perfectly straight in his dark uniform, exuding nothing but a terrifying air of aloofness and absolute, icy professional indifference.
 
For a second, I thought my heart was going to flatline. Thankfully, my survival instincts kicked in, and my mental fortitude held. I managed to force my complexion back to normal, locking my expression into a mask of total neutrality. I kept my head down until the very end of the briefing, when a voice completely devoid of emotion cut through the room.
 
"Selene. Come to my office immediately."
 
I forced out a quiet, "Yes, Alpha," and pinched my thigh hard under the desk to stop the shaking.
 
Once the room cleared, I clutched the project files tightly against my chest and walked down the isolated corridor leading to the Supreme Enforcer’s private office.
 
I stood outside the heavy iron-bound door, my hand hovering mid-air, completely hesitant to knock.
 
Killian’s office sat at the very end of a secluded hallway, entirely cut off from the bustling main workstation area. It was deathly quiet.
 
The man who had been my ex’s cousin two days ago, my reckless mistake last night, and my supreme commanding boss today... this man was single-handedly driving my inner wolf insane.
 
I took a series of deep, grounding breaths, plastering a look of grim determination on my face, and knocked.
 
"Come in." The voice was cold, crisp, and perfectly clear—nothing like the husky, gravelly growls that had completely shattered my restraint hours before.
 
I pushed the door open and stepped inside.
 
Killian didn't even look up at first. He glanced at me briefly before returning to his paperwork, treating me exactly like a complete stranger.
 
"Your workstation is positioned next to Summer’s," he stated smoothly. "Since you've just been assigned to the rogue case, you can direct any immediate operational questions to her." He paused for a fraction of a second, his dark eyes flicking up to mine. "Or you can ask me."
 
"Understood, Alpha. Is there anything else you require?" I asked, keeping my tone perfectly flat.
 
"Dismissed."
 
That was it?
 
I turned on my heel and walked out, the steady click of my boots against the stone floor sounding completely unhurried and composed.
 
~~~
 
After leaving Killian's office, I immediately dove into work. I was deep into analyzing the territory data when a sudden shadow fell over my desk. I looked up, and a spark of anger flared in my chest.
 
Xavier.
 
Aware that we were in the middle of a very high-security military office, I suppressed my anger, abruptly stood up, and marched out into the corridor to avoid a scene. But as I rounded the corner, the heavy doors of the central briefing room opened, and Killian stepped out, flanked by a group of senior captains.
 
Xavier, who was shadowing me closely, froze. His boyish swagger vanished, his posture stiffening instantly as he instinctively bowed his head. "Cousin," he muttered, his voice dropping an octave.
 
Killian’s eyes remained entirely expressionless as he scanned the two of us. He didn't offer a shred of familial warmth. "What is your business at headquarters?"
 
Xavier hesitated, his grip tightening as he looked at me. "I came to find my girlfriend."
 
I glared at him, my voice a sharp, low hiss. "We broke up, Xavier. Get it through your head."
 
A flash of erratic madness sparked in Xavier’s eyes. "You really want to cause a scene in front of the high command, Selene?"
 
"Do not bring your personal trash into my sectors," Killian cut in, his voice dropping into a cool, dangerous register as he looked directly at Xavier.
 
An invisible wave of pure, crushing Alpha aura rippled through the corridor, looming heavily over Xavier’s shoulders. Xavier shifted uncomfortably, a deep-seated, instinctual fear of his older cousin visibly holding him back. He didn't dare utter a single syllable until Killian turned and walked away with his captains.
 
The moment Killian was out of sight, Xavier’s cowardice turned right back into aggression. He lunged forward, grabbing my wrist in a tightly, and dragged me down the hallway without a word.
 
Knowing the severity of headquarters' rules, I didn't want to make a massive spectacle that would get me court-martialed on my first day, so I forced myself to cooperate temporarily, planning to tear him apart the second we hit the outer courtyard.
 
Instead, Xavier violently yanked me into an old, disused archive room at the furthest, darkest corner of the wing.
 
This place was completely isolated from the main operational sectors, and no one ever came down here. The second the heavy wooden door slammed shut, my compliance vanished. I violently ripped my wrist from his grip, my face turning deathly cold. "I told you, we are over."
 
Looking at him now, a bitter ache twisted in my gut. I HAD felt a genuine fondness for Xavier over the last six months. Even though he was a known playboy, he had treated me with an exceptional amount of care and consideration. I had genuinely believed an arrogant elite like him was capable of sincerity.
 
To find out that half a year of affection was nothing but a sickening gambling wager to break an untouchable omega... to say I wasn't heartbroken would be a lie and a fucking understatement.
 
Xavier looked disheveled, the remnants of his hangover making him pale, but a dangerous storm was brewing in his eyes. He gritted his teeth, stepping into my space. "Selene, it is always me who decides when a relationship is over. You are nothing but a packless nobody from a low-ranking rogue bloodline—where do you get off being so damn arrogant? I am the sole heir to the Beta line of the Southern pack. You should be down on your knees thanking me for even wanting to play with you. What gives you the right to say 'break up'? Even if we're going to end this, it'll happen when I'm thoroughly tired of you."
 
Before the last word even left his mouth, he lunged forward. His hand clamped violently around my chin, forcing my face up as he tried to forcefully press his lips against mine.
 
Shock and terror jammed in my throat as I realized he was actually going to use physical force against me. I thrashed against his grip, my claws instinctively lengthening as I snarled into his face, "Xavier, you've lost your mind!"
 
Xavier let out an arrogant, unhinged laugh, pinning me back against the heavy shelves. "You're the one who's crazy if you think you can walk away from me. I'll mark you right here today, and we'll see if you still have the pride to try and kill yourself tomorrow.”

Chapter three
Selene's POV
 
Xavier was a brute, Alpha who stood well over six feet tall and weighed a ton. I struggled in vain, my wrists pinned brutally behind my back by his massive hands.
 
I was completely immobilized, the sharp scent of his aggressive, uninvited pheromones making my stomach turn.
 
I thrashed against him, desperate to break his grip, but my resistance only seemed to make him more excited. A sick grin spread across his face as he locked me against him with one arm and grabbed my collar with his free hand, pulling hard.
 
The thin chiffon of my blouse gave way with a sharp rip, tearing from the neckline all the way down to my armpit. The cool air of the archives room hit my bare skin, and panic finally set in.
 
I was both angry and terrified. I knew that if I didn't call for help right now, it would be all over.
 
Xavier didn't care about the laws or human boundaries… All he wanted to do was dominate. Between protecting my pride and actual self-preservation, I chose the latter.
 
Just as I drew in a breath to scream, the heavy door of the document room was violently thrown open from the outside.
 
Xavier snapped his head around, his eyes flashing an ugly amber as he glared at the interruption.
 
The man standing in the doorway was framed by the harsh hallway light, tall, broad-shouldered, and radiating an immediate, undeniable authority.
 
It was Killian. He stood there, his dark eyes narrowed into slits, exuding a chilling aura that practically suffocated the room.
 
"I told you, don't cause me any trouble," Killian said, his voice dropping into a low, lethal baritone.
 
Looking at him, the tight knot of terror in my chest finally broke. Tears welled up in my eyes and streamed down my face.
 
I knew how pathetic I looked… shaking, exposed, my eyes probably wide and glassy, but I couldn't stop them.
 
Killian’s brows furrowed slightly as his gaze landed on my torn shirt. When he looked back at his cousin, his voice carried the crushing weight of a true Alpha command, full of undeniable pressure.
 
"Are you complaining about having too much freedom?"
 
The overwhelming aura Killian released finally forced Xavier to falter. He let out a low, frustrated growl, his grip loosening slightly.
 
He was furious and clearly unwilling to submit, but he didn't dare challenge Killian directly. You see, there were different types of Alphas. And while they all ruled the city, Dominant Alphas were at the top of the food chain. My gut told me that Killian was a dominant alpha because after a tense, agonizing second, Xavier let go of me and stepped back.
 
The moment I was free, my legs nearly gave out. I stumbled forward, practically throwing myself behind Killian’s broad back to hide. Without thinking, my fingers tightly gripped the fabric of his shirt at his waist, seeking any kind of anchor.
 
I held onto him like a lifeline. I was trembling so hard, gasping for air, that my hot breath sprayed directly onto his spine.
 
I felt Killian’s back stiffen under my touch, his muscles turning to stone, but he didn't pull away. Instead, he kept his icy glare locked on Xavier.
 
"Get lost," he ordered.
 
Xavier didn't need to be told twice. He threw one last resentful look in our direction before storming out and slamming the door behind him.
 
The second the door clicked shut, the adrenaline drained from my system. My knees buckled, and I collapsed against the wall, sliding down until I hit the floor.
 
My entire body shook uncontrollably from the shock. I forced myself to take deep breaths, opening and closing my numb, tingling hands, desperately trying to stop the frantic pounding of my heart.
 
Killian stood a few paces away. His gaze inadvertently swept down toward my exposed chest, but he quickly shifted his eyes toward the wall, his expression unreadable.
 
He pulled out his phone and dialed his secretary. "Do you have any extra shirts in the lounge? Send one to my office. If not, go to the mall downstairs and buy one. Get a size larger."
 
My heart stirred slightly at the gesture. I hadn't expected him to care. I looked up, my eyes meeting his dark, intense gaze just as he looked back down at me.
 
Realizing his eyes were tracing the torn fabric of my clothes again, I awkwardly clutched my ripped collar together and snapped my face away, my cheeks burning.
 
In the quiet of the archives room, the secretary’s frantic voice leaked through the phone speaker. "But sir, everyone in the conference room is waiting for you to start the board meeting..."
 
I blinked, a little surprised.
 
He had left a high-level meeting just to come down here?
 
Did he hear the commotion, or did his senses pick up that something was wrong?
 
I glanced up at him again. Whether it was just my imagination or the lingering relief of being saved, Killian didn't seem quite as ruthless and cold as he had been during our brief encounter this morning.
 
Sensing my eyes on him, Killian hung up the phone. His tone slipped back into that calm, even cadence, completely devoid of emotion. "I simply know what kind of garbage Xavier is. Don't overthink it. Thinking too much will only add to your troubles."
 
The warmth in my chest vanished instantly, replaced by a sudden rush of irritation. My face flushed deeper.
 
I forced myself to stand up, using the wall for support. I threw my shoulders back and held my head high, trying to channel the dignity of a proud wolf, even if I looked completely disheveled with a ruined blouse.
 
"Although I didn't think much of it, I still want to thank you for showing up when you did, Mr. CEO," I said, keeping my voice as steady as possible. "Also, please keep your cousin on a shorter leash. I am your subordinate, but I am also an employee of this company."
 
I knew the reality of my situation. With my current standing, it was impossible to hold someone like Xavier accountable through human resources or pack politics.
 
The matter would just be swept under the rug. The only thing I could do was demand that Killian restrain him under the guise of professional boundaries.
 
Killian didn't answer. His gaze drifted down to my wrists, which were already turning a dark, congested red from where Xavier had pinned them. He held my gaze for a second, then turned on his heel and left, closing the door quietly behind him.
 
The archives room fell into total silence. I stood there, stunned, before my legs gave out again. I stumbled over to a nearby chair and dropped into it, biting my lip so hard I tasted copper, trying to stop the tears from falling.
 
But they wouldn't stop. They kept overflowing, blurring my vision. I kept wiping them away with the back of my hand, forcing myself to take slow, agonizingly deep breaths to regain control.
 
A few minutes later, just as I was starting to think Killian had forgotten about me or had simply changed his mind, two sharp knocks echoed on the door.
 
It swung open, and Killian tossed a shopping bag onto the table inside. He didn't say a word, stepping right back out and shutting the door to give me privacy.
 
I took a deep breath, feeling a bit more grounded, and pulled the new shirt out of the bag. It was a crisp, white button-down. But as I quickly slipped into it and began doing up the front, my embarrassment returned full force.
 
The shirt was supposed to be a size large, but it was still too tight for me. The fabric strained against my curves, leaving a gap about the width of a thumb right between the buttons.
 
Left with no other choice, I grabbed a thick stack of project documents and held them tightly against my chest to cover the gap.
 
I walked over to a small mirror on the wall, making sure there were no tear stains or visible marks on my face, and finally left the document room.
 
~~~
 
By the time the clock struck five, any excitement I had about being promoted to the corporate headquarters had completely died.
 
Xavier’s attack had ruined my day, leaving me exhausted and on edge. But as I was gathering my things, a few of my new colleagues walked over, enthusiastically suggesting a welcome dinner to celebrate my first day.
 
Looking at their eager, smiling faces, every introverted instinct told me to refuse. I just wanted to crawl into a hole. But wanting to fit into the new department, I forced a smile and agreed.
 
We walked out to the lobby together, a large group of people chatting and pushing toward the elevator bay.
 
Since it was rush hour, everyone was trying to squeeze into the cars as tightly as possible. I stayed courteous, stepping back into the elevator to make more room for the people crowding in at the front.
 
But as I took another step backward, the air around me suddenly changed. I was instantly enveloped in a rich, heavy scent of dark cedar and winter woods.
 
My entire body went rigid. My wolf stirred instantly, recognizing that scent before my brain even did.
 
It was Killian. He was standing right behind me.
 
I froze, trying to anchor my feet to the floor to avoid touching him, but a sudden surge of people pushing into the front of the elevator shoved the crowd backward. The force sent me stumbling straight back, right into his chest.
 
For a split second, his large hands came up, gripping my waist instinctively to steady me before quickly letting go.
 
Even though the contact lasted only a heartbeat, my face flared bright red. The heat radiating from him was intense.
 
We were packed so tightly together that there wasn't even a fist of space between us.
 
I could feel his warm breath brushing against the back of my neck, and that intoxicating woody scent filled my lungs, instantly triggering vivid flashes of exactly what had happened between us the night before in the dark.
 
I clenched my toes inside my heels, dying of embarrassment, but I forced my expression to remain neutral, keeping up a casual conversation with my colleagues about where we should go for dinner.
 
My hair was pulled back into a simple ponytail, leaving my neck and ears completely exposed. I knew my ears were a dead giveaway—probably flushing a bright, telltale pink.
 
With him standing so close, any shift in my scent or body temperature from being flustered would be completely obvious to a predator like him.
 
I heard him take a slow, slightly heavier breath behind me, his chest expanding against my shoulder blades before he abruptly checked himself.
 
"It seems you already have the results of the first trial in your hands," Killian’s voice cut through the air.
 
It wasn't loud, and his tone was perfectly calm, but the sheer gravity of his voice carried an immense, suffocating pressure.
 
The noisy chatter in the elevator died instantly. My colleagues froze, their smiles vanishing as they silently panicked under the CEO’s gaze.
 
I didn't really care about his cold demeanor. Maybe because our relationship had already crossed a highly unprofessional line the night before, my fear of him as a boss was completely warped.
 
Instead, a different anxiety began to creep in.
 
Remembering how Xavier had trapped me in the archives room today, fear tightened in my throat. I couldn't go back to my apartment tonight.
 
I lived alone in a human neighborhood, and Xavier knew the address. There was no guarantee he wouldn't be waiting in the parking lot or outside my door to finish what he started.
 
Moving was the only safe option, but I wouldn't have time to look for a new place until the weekend. Where I was going to sleep for the next few days was a massive problem.
 
I had friends in the city, but I hated dragging people into my problems unless it was an absolute emergency.
 
‘Ding.’ The elevator finally reached the lobby, and the doors slid open. I snapped out of my thoughts, letting out a quiet breath of relief. I eagerly followed the crowd out into the open lobby, finally escaping the suffocating pull of that cedar scent.
 
The moment we hit the sidewalk, my colleagues exchanged quick, terrified glances and began to quietly disperse, making clumsy excuses about sudden work or family emergencies.
 
The terrifying aura Killian had radiated in the elevator had completely killed any appetite for a welcome dinner.
 
I watched them leave, not blaming them at all but as for me, I still needed to find a place to eat, and more importantly, a safe place to hide out tonight.

Chapter four
Selene's POV
 
After grabbing a quick dinner at a random noodle shop down the street, I went right back to the office building. I had already made up my mind.
 
Since there were only a few days left until the weekend, I could just find a cheap, short-term rental or a basic motel to get by for a couple of nights.
 
As for right now, going to a hotel meant sitting around doing nothing, so I figured I might as well stay at the company.
 
Reviewing the files and case documents would help me keep up with the project's progress and prove my worth to the new pack corporate hierarchy.
 
Many people were working overtime across the main floor, and I quickly got into work mode myself. I’ve always been highly career-oriented.
 
Once I get serious about a task, I become completely engrossed in it. I lost track of time so entirely that when I finally finished my target files and looked up, the entire office area was dead quiet and pitch black, save for the single light shining directly above my desk.
 
I glanced at the time on my phone and gasped. It was already eleven o'clock at night. I quickly opened a browser tab to search for nearby hotels that still had open check-ins.
 
"If you don't want to go back to your place, there are bedrooms upstairs that you can use," a smooth voice suddenly sounded from the shadows.
 
I jumped, my heart leaping into my throat as I snapped my head up.
 
It was Killian. He looked like he had just wrapped up a brutal mountain of paperwork himself and was finally preparing to leave for the night.
 
But a bedroom upstairs?
 
I blinked, a little confused by the setup of the penthouse levels. Before I could ask him to clarify, Killian kept his gaze fixed ahead and added, "I work a lot of overtime, so I often sleep here at the company."
 
I nodded knowingly. The entire corporate headquarters of Silver Law Firm was practically his territory, so it wasn't surprising at all that a powerful billionaire Alpha would design a luxury private lounge for himself on the restricted upper floors.
 
Although our dynamic was incredibly awkward after what had happened between us, I didn't hesitate for a second when faced with the choice between staying inside the secure, heavily guarded corporate building or a sketchy, unprotected short-term hotel. Xavier could easily track me to a public motel, but he wouldn't dare breach Killian's private space.
 
"Thanks," I murmured, genuinely relieved.
 
"The 20th floor. The door password is 4792."
 
I watched him walk toward the private executive elevator. He actually just gave me the password directly.
 
Isn't that a bit too careless for an Alpha who guards his privacy so fiercely? I thought to myself.
 
Shaking off the thought, I quickly packed my laptop into my bag, turned off the last overhead light, and clocked out for the night.
 
The two of us left the quiet office suite one after the other, meeting up at the secure elevator bank.
 
I pressed the call button, and the elevator arrived almost instantly with a soft chime. I was still incredibly grateful to Killian for providing me with a safe haven from his rogue cousin, so I turned to him with a polite smile to say goodbye before stepping into the car.
 
But then, to my surprise, he followed me right into the elevator.
 
I paused for a second, my fingers hovering over the panel before I subconsciously pressed the button for the 20th floor.
 
As the metallic doors slid closed, trapping us in the small space, I kept glancing to my left out of the corner of my eye.
 
I desperately wanted to ask why he was coming up too, but I couldn't find the right words without sounding completely presumptuous.
 
Killian seemed to sense my internal panic. Without looking at me, he calmly said, "I usually stay at the company anyway. I only went back to the estate yesterday because it was inconvenient to bring you directly to the office."
 
I forced a stiff smile, staring hard at the illuminated floor numbers changing above the door while my inner voice roared in frustration.
 
Why didn't you say so earlier?!
 
Why did you just hand over the password like that?!
 
He had completely led me to believe I was going up to the penthouse to sleep alone.
 
What was I supposed to do now?
 
Demand to go back down?
 
If I bailed halfway through the ride, wouldn't I seem incredibly petty, like I was judging his intentions by my own frantic standards?
 
My mind was in an absolute frenzy, but before I could make a final decision, the elevator dinged loudly as we reached our destination.
 
Killian stepped out into the grand, dimly lit penthouse foyer first, leaving behind a completely nonchalant explanation. "I gave you the password so you can come and go easily over the next few days. You should be able to find a permanent place and move this weekend."
 
Does this man have actual mind-reading abilities? I thought, gritting my teeth. Unfortunately, I was completely cornered by my own safety concerns, so I could only swallow my anxiety, endure the mental torment, and follow him inside.
 
However, a wave of immense relief washed over me the moment I stepped through the main doors. The interior space was absolutely massive, sprawling across the entire top floor.
 
With a place this big, I was absolutely certain I would have my own private room to sleep in without being anywhere near him.
 
Feeling a bit more relaxed, I bent down at the entryway to re-tie the leather straps of my high heels, which had come loose during the walk.
 
As I did, I heard his deep voice echo from just a few feet ahead of me. "There are several empty guest rooms down the hall. You can choose whichever one you like."
 
I stood up straight, but before I could even open my mouth to say thank you, a small white object shot out from my chest with a sharp ‘ping’, flying through the air and hitting Killian squarely in the middle of his back.
 
The two of us instantly froze, facing each other in the quiet hallway.
 
I glanced down out of the corner of my eye, and my breath caught instantly in my throat.
 
It had ripped.
 
The straining button on the front of the replacement shirt he had bought me had finally snapped under the pressure of my chest, completely popping off and leaving the front of the shirt gaping open. I stood there, utterly paralyzed with mortification.
 
Killian turned around slowly, his dark eyes sweeping down over my exposed collarbone and the gap in the fabric before he looked away, his voice entirely light and even. "This shirt is clearly a bit too small for you."
 
I blushed instantly, a fierce heat rushing up my neck until my face was bright red to the roots of my hair. I felt like I had been repeatedly dunked in boiling water.
 
Without a word, I silently scrambled to scoop the broken button off the hardwood floor, held my handbag horizontally across my chest like a shield, and casually plunged into the very first bedroom door I could reach to escape his gaze.
 
"That room is..."
 
I heard his voice start to caution me from the hallway, but I didn't care. I was fleeing in absolute disarray. I slammed the door behind me, only to immediately realize what was wrong. The room smelled overwhelmingly of dark cedar, leather, and pure Alpha dominance. It was distinctly his.
 
My face felt like it was about to bleed from sheer embarrassment and the overwhelming scent of him. Turning on my heel, I bolted right back out into the hallway, completely losing my composure.
 
I was moving so fast and was so thoroughly mortified that I didn't even notice Killian was still standing right outside the frame. I ran headfirst straight into his broad chest.
 
"Ah..." I gasped as the impact rattled my face. My nose throbbed painfully, and the sudden sting instantly triggered my tear ducts, causing my eyes to well up with involuntary tears.
 
I subconsciously looked up at him through a blurry, watery gaze, my eyes sparkling with a mix of pain and intense shyness.
 
My naturally fair skin was completely flushed like ripe cherries, making me look utterly defenseless, delicate, and entirely exposed.
 
As I stood trapped against him, the natural, sweet fragrance of my skin flared from the stress, completely enveloping him in the narrow hallway.
 
I felt Killian's breathing stutter, turning slightly heavier as he felt my soft shape pressed directly into his arms. His dark gaze gradually deepened, a dangerous, primal spark flickering in the depths of his eyes.
 
"This is my room," he murmured, his voice dropping into a low, raspy register.
 
Hearing him speak like that made my heart pound frantically against my ribs. He sounded less like a cold, distant corporate CEO and more like something inexplicably alluring.
 
My pulse raced. I bit my lip hard, letting out a faint, embarrassed "Oh," before I twisted out of his grip, turned around, and quickly slipped into the guest bedroom next door, shutting the door firmly behind me.
 
~~~
 
Once safely inside the proper guest room, I rushed through washing my face and quickly climbed into the large bed, desperate to put the chaotic evening behind me.
 
However, the moment I pulled the heavy comforter up to my chin knock echoed against the wood of my door.
 
My muscles tensed up involuntarily. I gripped the edge of the blanket tightly, hesitating in the dark for a long moment before raising my voice to call out, "What's wrong?"
 
"I brought some ointment for your wrists. You might need it," Killian’s voice drifted through the door.
 
I sat up slowly, shifting the covers aside.
 
The words he spoke were cool, aloof, and completely devoid of any underlying desire or hidden meaning.
 
His tone left absolutely no room for a wandering imagination, making the intense tension of the previous night feel like nothing more than a fever dream.
 
I shook my head vigorously to clear the lingering fog from my brain and looked down at my hands.
 
Xavier had gripped my skin with so much force during the struggle in the archives room that my skin was covered in ugly, dark bruises and shallow scratches where his nails had dug in.
 
"Just a second, I'm coming," I called out.
 
I quickly smoothed down my clothes, slipped my feet into my shoes, and walked over to swing the door open.
 
Killian was standing there holding a small tube of medical ointment. He handed it over without a word, gave me a brief nod, and turned right back around to walk to his own room.
 
I stood in the doorway, staring down at the unopened tube in my hand, feeling a sudden warmth in my chest.
 
No matter how cold or intimidating he chose to be, Killian had gone out of his way to protect and look after me today.
 
~~~
 
Despite the safety of the penthouse, I didn't sleep well at all. The trauma from Xavier’s attack followed me into the dark, plaguing me with restless, exhausting nightmares all through the night.
 
When my alarm finally went off in the morning, my head felt heavy and my brain was completely groggy.
 
Still, I forced myself out of bed and navigated my way into the kitchen. Part of it was because my stomach was completely empty, but the larger part was because I wanted to find a way to properly thank Killian for taking me in when I had nowhere else to go.
 
I found a wealth of fresh groceries stocked in the massive stainless-steel refrigerator. I pulled out ingredients and quickly set to work, losing myself in the rhythm of cooking.
 
A short while later, the sound of footsteps signaled Killian entering the space.
 
I didn't see him look at me, but I adjusted the apron around my waist, my hair loosely tied up with a few stray strands falling gently around my face as the morning sunlight streamed through the floor-to-ceiling windows behind me.
 
I plated the food and turned around to carry the dishes to the long dining table, only to find him standing much closer than I expected, watching me silently.
 
The sudden sight of him startled me so much that I nearly dropped the plates, freezing in my tracks.
 
Seeing him staring at me with that unreadable expression, I felt a familiar shyness creep up my neck. I quickly cleared my throat to explain myself. "I noticed you had a lot of fresh groceries in the fridge. I know someone like you definitely won't accept rent money from me, but I really don't feel comfortable staying here completely for free. I'm actually a pretty decent cook, so please consider breakfast as my payment for the room, okay?"
 
In truth, when I had first opened the refrigerator and seen it piled high with fresh fruits, vegetables, and high-quality ingredients, I simply couldn't resist.
 
I honestly hadn't expected a powerful, solitary Alpha who seemed entirely unaccustomed to domestic life to keep such a warm, homey, and fully stocked kitchen.
 
Killian didn't show much expression on his handsome face. He merely gave a slight nod and said, "Thank you for your hard work," in a light, even tone before consciously moving over to take a seat at the table.
 
I set down the meal I had prepared: a golden scallion and ham egg roll, a plate of crispy shrimp potstickers, and a steaming bowl of traditional savory congee with preserved egg and lean pork. It was a simple, comforting, yet deeply satisfying breakfast.
 
He ate efficiently and in total silence. Once he finished his portion, Killian set his chopsticks down on the rest, pulled a linen napkin to slowly wipe his mouth, and said emotionlessly, "It tasted very good."
 
His delivery was completely flat, merely stating an objective fact, exactly the same way he had handed over the five million dollar check after our first night together.
 
Over the past two days, I had managed to get a general idea of what kind of temperament my new boss possessed. If I had to describe him to anyone, I would say he was completely emotionless and frighteningly calm at all times.
 
That kind of detached personality made him an absolute terror in the legal world, his cold-blooded nature allowed him to rationally analyze and dismantle every single variable in a case without ever letting personal feelings get in the way.
 
He truly deserved his reputation as the undefeated warrior of the high court.
 
Since there was absolutely no personal emotion tied to his compliment, I didn't let it fluster me. I simply listened to the praise and offered a polite, professional smile. "I'm glad you liked it."
 
Killian stood up from the table, his sharp eyes dropping for a fraction of a second to the front of my chest.
 
Because the button had popped last night, I had been forced to use a thin piece of spare twine to hastily tie the fabric together, and the makeshift fix was barely holding the shirt closed against my skin.
 
He buttoned his suit jacket and checked his watch. "I've already had a selection of professional attire delivered and placed in the living room for you. As a practicing lawyer, I shouldn't need to elaborate on the importance of proper courtroom attire."
 
He paused at the edge of the kitchen, turning back slightly. "There's no need for you to clear the table or wash the dishes. A housekeeper will be here shortly to handle the cleaning."
 
I felt a sudden flush of embarrassment heat my cheeks. My formal suits for actual court appearances were incredibly high quality and immaculate. It was only my regular, everyday office wear that was a bit more ordinary.
 
"I..." I started, wanting to say thank you, but the word caught in my throat.
 
Watching his tall silhouette vanish out the front door, I slowly swallowed the rest of my sentence.
 
Even though he had mentioned a housekeeper was on the way, I still gathered the plates and carried them over to the sink to wash them out of sheer politeness.
 
After all, regardless of our strange history, this was still his home, and I refused to be a burden.

Chapter one
Selene
 
Birthdays weren't really a big deal for me.
 
But for my twenty-fifth birthday, I wanted to do something completely out of character that would leave everyone's gaze on the floor. I wore a crimson silk dress that hugged every curve of my body, making my skin look stark white against the bold fabric.
 
At 7 p.m., I walked into the largest club in the city..
 
The indoor pool, the she-wolves in bikinis, the passionate kissing, and the deafening music made me instantly uncomfortable, but I endured it. After all, this was a birthday party that Xavier had specially organized for me.
 
After asking around, I finally found Xavier’s private room and thankfully it was much quieter than the noisy, bustling chaos outside, which let me breathe a little easier.
 
Just as I was about to push open the door, a loud laugh came from inside.
 
"Wow, Xavier, you actually reeled her in after half a year? I thought a chaste, virtuous woman like Selene wouldn't be seduced by you. I admit defeat this time. I'll transfer a hundred thousand to your account tonight."
 
Another guy laughed. "You're already conceding before you've even reached base? I don't care, I'm only giving in when it's confirmed tomorrow morning."
 
The room filled with rowdy laughter, but the world around me went eerily quiet. I stared blankly at the doorknob, all my warmth I felt and was feeling gradually turning to ice.
 
The discussions inside didn't stop though.
 
"Is Young Master Xavier really planning to sleep with her and then dump her? Selene might be an omega from the outer territories, but she's still the academy beauty. Perfect figure, top grades, and most importantly—she's still untouched."
 
"Her family is poor, from a low-ranking rogue lineage by the way. No matter how good she is, a girl like that is only meant to be played with."
 
I felt my blood boil and my stomach churn. I trembled slightly, my nails digging deep into my palms as I took sharp breaths to suppress my rising fury. But when I heard that familiar voice, I couldn't hold back anymore.
 
"It's hard to say," Xavier said. "I'm not in a rush to choose a fated mate. I can play around for another two years."
 
I threw the door open with a loud click, the faint hallway glow shone directly on me, making the red dress dazzlingly bright in the dim room.
 
The sounds inside abruptly stopped.
 
Xavier looked toward the door, his smug expression freezing for a split second. Then, he stood up with a smooth smile, acting as if nothing had happened. "Why did you come up here by yourself? I was just about to go down and pick you up."
 
I didn't let myself show a single shred of emotion. I just kept a casual, contemptuous smile on my lips. "Do you know why you couldn't seduce me in half a year, Xavier? Because I'm a germaphobe, and your scent is too freaking dirty."
 
Xavier stood there, stunned, until I turned and disappeared down the hall. Only then did he snap out of his daze, clenching his fists tightly. He grabbed a wine glass from the table and smashed it violently on the floor, furious. "Selene!"
 
~~~
 
Everything went to shit after that but when I left there, I didn't go home immediately. Instead, I went into a nearby rogue-friendly bar. It wasn't that I was intentionally trying to get blackout drunk. I just had nothing else to do, so I ordered a pitcher of liquor and sipped it slowly, watching the lively crowd on the dance floor like an outsider. I finally left, staggering unsteadily, when I almost fell asleep in my seat.
 
As I passed a traffic light, I spotted an SUV that looked structurally like Xavier’s, but when I got closer, I saw that it wasn't.
 
But still, a vehicle like this could only be bought by someone with terrifying power, not to mention that the design was incredibly sleek. Older Alphas generally didn't drive this kind of car. At that moment, under the heavy influence of the alcohol, a twisted desire for revenge flared up in my heart.
 
I stepped forward and knocked firmly on the dark window and someone rolled down the window.
 
I pulled on the handle, ready to get into the passenger seat.
 
He must have caught the faint scent of alcohol on me, and seeing that the red light was about to change, he unlocked the door and let me scramble inside.
 
"Xavier isn't with you?" his deep, authoritative baritone filled the car. "I'll have him come pick you up."
 
I panicked the second I heard Xavier's name, completely forgetting to wonder why the driver of a random car knew about my relationship with him. But I was too drunk to care.
 
I gripped his arm tightly, though I forced my tone to sound completely nonchalant. "We broke up."
 
"Then I'll take you home. Where is your pack-house?"
 
After a long moment, having received no reply from me, his turned his head and smiled meaningfully.
 
~~~
 
I vaguely felt someone carry me and lay me down on a massive bed. I forced my eyes halfway open and met a pair of piercing, starry eyes.
 
'He looks dangerously good,' I thought to myself.
 
The man exuded a terrifyingly noble aura, his broad arms brimming with raw, masculine Lycan strength. Unlike Xavier’s boyish charm, this man was mature and deadly—clearly someone who walked the highest echelons of power and wealth in the supernatural world. He was like a walking hormonal poison, capable of captivating a she-wolf without her even realizing it.
 
'Is it just my imagination? Why does he look so familiar?'
 
I stared intently, my eyes misty with unshed tears, my cheeks flushed with a drunken blush. I looked captivating, yet my wide eyes remained pure and gentle.
 
His voice carried a low, warning growl. "What you're doing right now is dangerous."
 
Drunk and confused, I didn't care about the danger. I wrapped my arms tightly around his waist, looking both innocent and completely clingy.
 
His Adam's apple bobbed. With a low sound, he rolled onto the bed, pinning my hands flat above my head. His deep voice carried a dangerous hint of seduction. "Who am I?"
 
I sniffed the air weakly, my eyes sparkling under his weight. "You smell very nice... like cedar and frost."
 
His chest tightened. He freed one hand, violently loosening his tie and tossing it aside, then leaned down and kissed me tenderly. His kisses traveled from my lips to my jaw, then down to my ear, tasting me slowly, carefully trying to control his rhythm. But a hint of his usual, icy clarity remained in his eyes.
 
A tingling sensation shot through my entire body. I unconsciously murmured a soft, tender whimper, a sound so gentle it completely shattered his restraint when it hit his ears.
 
I felt as if I were on a roller coaster, my heart pounding wildly back and forth. Then, a sharp pain brought me back to my senses for a single, gasping moment, followed by a hazy, dreamlike feeling as if I were floating on clouds.
 
When I finally opened my eyes again, it was broad daylight.
 
But waking up brought an endless, crushing wave of regret.
 
Yes, I was filled with deep, sickening regret. A perfectly rational woman had made a terrible mistake and given herself to a stranger on a drunken whim. I wanted to slap myself.
 
"You're awake."
 
My body tensed instantly, and my heart pounded like a war drum. But my mind immediately locked onto a decision: things had already gone this far, and I was the one who had taken the initiative, so I had to preserve the absolute last bit of my dignity.
 
I sat up, pulling the covers over myself and forcing a calm, composed face, though I was inwardly cursing my own stupidity. "Last night... it was consensual. And we'll never see each other again."
 
Unfortunately, my voice choked up before I could finish the sentence. My gaze finally focused on the man's face, and my mind reeled as if struck by lightning.
 
The towering, slender figure, the unapproachable aura, and that calm, analytical gaze left me completely bewildered.
 
I had met Killian once a few months ago at a high-ranking pack summit, but mature Alphas with an ascetic, deadly air always leave a deep impression. I remembered him instantly.
 
This was Xavier’s older cousin. He was the Supreme Alpha of the entire Northern Coalition—the most ruthless legal and martial authority in the werewolf world. He was completely invincible in pack tribunals and enjoyed a terrifying reputation.
 
This man, revered as an unfeeling god by the packs, was so calm and wise right now that I couldn't even reconcile him with the wolfish, aggressive predator from last night.
 
It was completely outrageous.
 
I suddenly felt dizzy. I instinctively braced myself against the mattress, and the obviously oversized silk pajamas he had put me in slipped down my shoulders, revealing a glimpse of my chest.
 
I hurriedly pulled the collar back up, my face burning with acute embarrassment—entirely unaware that the man sitting by the bed was giving me a much deeper look.

"Just a second, I'm coming," I called out.
 
I quickly smoothed down my clothes, slipped my feet into my shoes, and walked over to swing the door open.
 
Killian was standing there holding a small tube of medical ointment. He handed it over without a word, gave me a brief nod, and turned right back around to walk to his own room.
 
I stood in the doorway, staring down at the unopened tube in my hand, feeling a sudden warmth in my chest.
 
No matter how cold or intimidating he chose to be, Killian had gone out of his way to protect and look after me today.
 
~~~
 
Despite the safety of the penthouse, I didn't sleep well at all. The trauma from Xavier’s attack followed me into the dark, plaguing me with restless, exhausting nightmares all through the night.
 
When my alarm finally went off in the morning, my head felt heavy and my brain was completely groggy.
 
Still, I forced myself out of bed and navigated my way into the kitchen. Part of it was because my stomach was completely empty, but the larger part was because I wanted to find a way to properly thank Killian for taking me in when I had nowhere else to go.
 
I found a wealth of fresh groceries stocked in the massive stainless-steel refrigerator. I pulled out ingredients and quickly set to work, losing myself in the rhythm of cooking.
 
A short while later, the sound of footsteps signaled Killian entering the space.
 
I didn't see him look at me, but I adjusted the apron around my waist, my hair loosely tied up with a few stray strands falling gently around my face as the morning sunlight streamed through the floor-to-ceiling windows behind me.
 
I plated the food and turned around to carry the dishes to the long dining table, only to find him standing much closer than I expected, watching me silently.
 
The sudden sight of him startled me so much that I nearly dropped the plates, freezing in my tracks.
 
Seeing him staring at me with that unreadable expression, I felt a familiar shyness creep up my neck. I quickly cleared my throat to explain myself. "I noticed you had a lot of fresh groceries in the fridge. I know someone like you definitely won't accept rent money from me, but I really don't feel comfortable staying here completely for free. I'm actually a pretty decent cook, so please consider breakfast as my payment for the room, okay?"
 
In truth, when I had first opened the refrigerator and seen it piled high with fresh fruits, vegetables, and high-quality ingredients, I simply couldn't resist.
 
I honestly hadn't expected a powerful, solitary Alpha who seemed entirely unaccustomed to domestic life to keep such a warm, homey, and fully stocked kitchen.
 
Killian didn't show much expression on his handsome face. He merely gave a slight nod and said, "Thank you for your hard work," in a light, even tone before consciously moving over to take a seat at the table.
 
I set down the meal I had prepared: a golden scallion and ham egg roll, a plate of crispy shrimp potstickers, and a steaming bowl of traditional savory congee with preserved egg and lean pork. It was a simple, comforting, yet deeply satisfying breakfast.
 
He ate efficiently and in total silence. Once he finished his portion, Killian set his chopsticks down on the rest, pulled a linen napkin to slowly wipe his mouth, and said emotionlessly, "It tasted very good."
 
His delivery was completely flat, merely stating an objective fact, exactly the same way he had handed over the five million dollar check after our first night together.
 
Over the past two days, I had managed to get a general idea of what kind of temperament my new boss possessed. If I had to describe him to anyone, I would say he was completely emotionless and frighteningly calm at all times.
 
That kind of detached personality made him an absolute terror in the legal world, his cold-blooded nature allowed him to rationally analyze and dismantle every single variable in a case without ever letting personal feelings get in the way.
 
He truly deserved his reputation as the undefeated warrior of the high court.
 
Since there was absolutely no personal emotion tied to his compliment, I didn't let it fluster me. I simply listened to the praise and offered a polite, professional smile. "I'm glad you liked it."
 
Killian stood up from the table, his sharp eyes dropping for a fraction of a second to the front of my chest.
 
Because the button had popped last night, I had been forced to use a thin piece of spare twine to hastily tie the fabric together, and the makeshift fix was barely holding the shirt closed against my skin.
 
He buttoned his suit jacket and checked his watch. "I've already had a selection of professional attire delivered and placed in the living room for you. As a practicing lawyer, I shouldn't need to elaborate on the importance of proper courtroom attire."
 
He paused at the edge of the kitchen, turning back slightly. "There's no need for you to clear the table or wash the dishes. A housekeeper will be here shortly to handle the cleaning."
 
I felt a sudden flush of embarrassment heat my cheeks. My formal suits for actual court appearances were incredibly high quality and immaculate. It was only my regular, everyday office wear that was a bit more ordinary.
 
"I..." I started, wanting to say thank you, but the word caught in my throat.
 
Watching his tall silhouette vanish out the front door, I slowly swallowed the rest of my sentence.
 
Even though he had mentioned a housekeeper was on the way, I still gathered the plates and carried them over to the sink to wash them out of sheer politeness.
 
After all, regardless of our strange history, this was still his home, and I refused to be a burden.
